messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT: Elevated error rates observed for PrivateLink endpoints in eu-west-3 AZ-C (region: eu-west-3c). Alert triggered by 5xx surge and DNS resolution failures. Paging oncall.

sara-nguyen: seeing a bunch of 502/504s from customer traffic hitting pl-azc-prod. Error spike started ~1739004280. Also seeing repeated NXDOMAIN / SERVFAIL for customer service hostnames via our resolver.

mike-rojas: confirmed on telemetry. Per-host error rate up to 18% for PrivateLink endpoints in the AZ-C pool. Latency also spiking. Route churn logs show frequent withdraws from the local route reflector.

ashley-chen: tagging netops. @tian-lu are we seeing BGP flaps between edge rtrs in AZ-C and the peering fabric? Also which customers reported impact so I can call out to CS?

tian-lu: looking. BGP sessions A->R3 show repeated UPDATE/NOTIFICATION exchanges since ~1739004200, looks like session reset pattern. Might be CPU spike on the AZ-C ToR that hosts the vrrp/peering. Pulling kernel logs from the node.

netops-bot: Netops alert: Core switch azc-core-2 reported High Interrupt (IRQ) due to control-plane storm. Automated telemetry collected: /var/log/syslog excerpt:
```
Mar 15 17:31:52 azc-core-2 kernel: BUG: soft lockup in CPU#3
Mar 15 17:31:53 azc-core-2 bgpd[2345]: neighbor 10.10.23.1 down: Connection reset by peer
```

sara-nguyen: customer-impact list: AcmePayments (PL endpoint id: pl-acme-01), FinApps (pl-fin-03), internal-service-metrics (pl-intmet-2). CS already opened tickets. I'll DM support owners.

mike-rojas: quick mitigation idea: fail traffic for PL endpoints in AZ-C to AZ-B replicas (we have warmed replicas in AZ-B). Can we trigger routing policy to prefer AZ-B while we remediate? That reduces latency but keeps availability.

tian-lu: we can do a policy push. Two options: (1) short BGP prepends on azc-local to de-preference AZ-C (fast) or (2) update our LB routing policies to shift PL endpoints to AZ-B (app-layer steer, safer). Prepend has faster propagation but could cause asymmetric routing.

ashley-chen: prefer App-layer steer if it can be done quickly. Risk of asymmetric path is annoying for TLS mutual auth customers. How long to push app policy?

mike-rojas: app policy push is ~5-8 minutes to propagate via control plane; prepping for canary (10% to AZ-B first). I can flip 10% -> 50% -> 100% in increments.

tian-lu: meanwhile I'm pulling the crash dump from azc-core-2 and will try to reboot the forwarding plane if CPU lockup persists. Netops will coordinate maintenance window but we need emergency action.

sara-nguyen: can we also flush DNS negative cache for the customer resolvers? Their clients are getting NXDOMAIN; negative TTL is long (300s). If we shift endpoints to AZ-B the resolver edges should start getting healthy answers but negative cache may persist.

mike-rojas: implementing canary shift now: updating routing via console -> PL route policy -> canary 10% to AZ-B.

incident-bot: ACTION_LOG: mike-rojas started canary shift at 1739004350. Change id: change-PL-1739004350.

ashley-chen: monitoring. Observability: error rate for pl-acme-01 falling from 18% -> 6% for canary traffic. DNS NXDOMAIN still showing for some resolvers (legacy recursors).

tian-lu: core node azc-core-2 is unstable; kernel OOM/softlockup appears correlated to a device driver bug on recent image. Netops recommends rolling azc-core-2 out of the pool and replacing with standby. Initiating drain of L3 sessions.

netops-bot: Netops task created: NET-3487 - Replace azc-core-2 and failover BGP sessions. ETA 30m for hardware swap. Operator: tian-lu.

sara-nguyen: customer comms draft: "We are investigating an elevated error rate impacting PrivateLink endpoints in eu-west-3 AZ-C. We have shifted traffic to AZ-B as a mitigation and are replacing an unstable network device in AZ-C. We will update in 30m." Should I send?

ashley-chen: send to affected customer list, mark as "intermittent but partial mitigation in place". Include support ticket links.

mike-rojas: increasing canary to 50% now (change-PL-1739004378).

incident-bot: ACTION_LOG: mike-rojas increased canary to 50% at 1739004378.

ashley-chen: metrics: pl-fin-03 errors down to 2%. pl-acme-01 still shows some 5xx on the non-canary subset. DNS negative cache entries are expiring soon per TTL.

tian-lu: drain complete for azc-core-2, initiating device replacement now. Replacing control-plane module, will monitor.

netops-bot: Update NET-3487: replacement in-progress, expected BGP reconvergence while switch is swapped. Keep canary until reconverge completes.

mike-rojas: moving to 100% AZ-B now (change-PL-1739004395) to reduce blast radius while repair ongoing.

incident-bot: ACTION_LOG: mike-rojas set traffic to 100% AZ-B at 1739004395.

sara-nguyen: CS update sent at 1739004398. Customers acknowledged and asked for ETA; gave 30-45m and offered call if they see further issues.

tian-lu: replacement complete, control-plane stable on new module. BGP sessions re-established cleanly at 1739004402. No further kernel lockups observed for 3s (monitoring continuing).

ashley-chen: can we now safely shift traffic back to AZ-C in controlled manner? We should also flush DNS caches for edge resolvers where we can to avoid NXDOMAIN persistence.

mike-rojas: will canary 10% back to AZ-C, watch for 5xx spike. If stable, increase.

incident-bot: ACTION_LOG: mike-rojas canary 10% AZ-C at 1739004403.

ashley-chen: monitoring shows no spike; incrementing to 50%.

tian-lu: verifying BGP flaps cleared. No route withdraws in last 20s. Kernel logs look clean. I'll leave maintenance ticket open for follow-up root cause after-hours.

sara-nguyen: handing off to next oncall for follow-up and RCA: @oncall-next - summary: PrivateLink endpoints in eu-west-3 AZ-C experienced control-plane device CPU lockups causing BGP session resets and DNS negative caching. We shifted traffic to AZ-B and replaced azc-core-2. Customers partially impacted; mitigated. Links: NET-3487, change-PL-1739004350. Please continue to monitor for 2 hours and run deep packet captures if flaps reappear.

oncall-next: acknowledged. I'll own the RCA and coordinate postmortem. Leaving a TODO list: collect kernel dmesg, collect bgp update logs, ping/traceroute from edge, check firmware on azc-core-2 spare. Also push DNS cache flush to edge recursors where possible.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated - partial service restore confirmed at 1739004405. Incident will be transitioned to follow-up and RCA. If further degradation observed reopen thread."
